modelset.benchmark_in_mcs.spec: series whose Model Confidence Set CONTAINS seasonal_naive (alpha=0.1, absolute loss, block=3, B=2000). The complement is the count in which the one structurally different candidate is correctly eliminated -- so the tied sets are almost entirely composed of the five near-collinear models.

cites: S3.1 body: how similar are the candidate models
modelset.benchmark_last.spec: series in which seasonal_naive has the WORST pooled mean loss of the models that actually competed on that series (six today, but compared against each series' own model count, not a fixed number). The curated series are pre-seasonally-adjusted by their source agency, so a 12-month seasonal-naive forecast is a deliberately weak reference, not a rival.

cites: S3.1 body: how similar are the candidate models
modelset.benchmark_ratio_max.spec: largest ratio of seasonal_naive's pooled mean loss to the best model's, across series

modelset.elimination_identical_sets.spec: curated series on which the raw-mean elimination rule (this paper's default) and HLN's e_R rule -- the rule HLN pair with the T_R range statistic, and the rule arch's MCS(method='R') implements -- return the IDENTICAL surviving set (same models, not merely the same cardinality), at alpha=0.1, block=3, B=2000. Bears directly on S4.1: on the series where they differ, e_R reproduces arch's set, so the elimination rule IS part of the residual arch-vs-ours disagreement (the rest is arch's stationary-bootstrap default plus, on the population sweep, a residual that survives matching both -- see mcsarch.*_bootstrap_matched / *_fully_matched).

modelset.loss_corr_median.cross_check: model_set_audit.csv: np.median(all pooled pairwise loss correlations)
modelset.loss_corr_median.spec: median pairwise Pearson correlation of the ANNUAL LOSS series among the five non-benchmark models, pooled over all series and pairs. Loss rather than forecast level on purpose: two forecasts of the same trending series correlate near 1 mechanically, so a forecast-level correlation would overstate the similarity.

modelset.loss_corr_min.spec: smallest pairwise annual-loss correlation among the five non-benchmark models, over every (series, pair) -- the least similar any two substantive candidates ever are. Attained on BOPGEXP (see model_set_audit.csv's per-series loss_corr_min column: min(that column) reproduces this value, since both are min(pooled pair_r) -- the median column alone could not re-derive it).

cites: S13.2: set size versus sample size
modelset.mean_mcs_monthly_b24.spec: mean |MCS| on the native monthly panels at bootstrap block=24. Emitted BESIDE the block=1 value on purpose: mean |MCS| falls from 3.92 (annual) to 3.17 at short blocks but RISES to this value at long ones, because a long block cuts the number of independent blocks back down. Quoting only the falling end would overstate the sample-size reading.
